title: Worked example: a SIP through a fall
objectives: Work the V-shaped fall example and explain why the SIP ends ahead.
Say what the SIP investor did differently: they kept going.
body_md:
All examples below are illustrative: simplified price paths and assumed returns, not real fund data and not forecasts. Example 1: a SIP through a fall. A fund's NAV falls steadily from ₹100 to ₹60 over 12 months, then recovers to ₹100 over the next 12 months. Lump sum at the start: ₹2,40,000 invested → ₹2,40,000 at month 24 (NAV back to ₹100) → 0%. SIP of ₹10,000 a month: ₹2,40,000 invested → about ₹3,07,000 at month 24 → about +28%.

| Investor | Invested | Value at month 24 (NAV back to ₹100) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lump sum at the start | ₹2,40,000 | ₹2,40,000 | 0% |
| SIP of ₹10,000 a month | ₹2,40,000 | ≈ ₹3,07,000 | ≈ +28% |

The SIP investor bought more units when prices were low. The fall that felt like “the wrong time” was actually what made the SIP work, but only because the investor kept going.

> **Investor takeaway:** Bad timing hurts less than stopping, selling or never starting.
example: ₹10,000 a month for 24 months through NAV ₹100 → ₹60 → ₹100: ₹2.4 lakh invested, about ₹3.07 lakh at the end.
say: The same amount buys more units when prices are low.
The fall only helped because the investor kept going.
never: A lump sum at the start beats a SIP through a fall.

check.q: Why can a SIP end up ahead after a V-shaped fall?
o: The same amount buys more units at low prices
check.why: The same amount buys more units at low prices. Low prices mean more units, which lowers the average cost.

check.q: In Example 1, why did the SIP end at about +28% while the lump sum ended at 0%?
o: The same amount bought more units at lower prices
check.why: The SIP investor bought more units when prices were low.

check.q: What condition made the SIP's fall work for it?
o: The investor kept going through the fall
check.why: The fall that felt like “the wrong time” was actually what made the SIP work, but only because the investor kept going.
